heroHeadline: Burhan Formally Derecognizes RSF as State Institution; Nyala Aerial Campaign Enters Day 4 — Hemedti's TSC Deputy Role to Be Stripped
heroSubtitle: On Day 1129, al-Burhan issued an executive order formally derecognizing the RSF as a state institution, cutting off RSF soldiers from government payroll and clearing the path for Hemedti's imminent removal as Transitional Sovereignty Council deputy (Malik Agar named replacement, May 19). RSF soldiers clashed with SAF-aligned forces at the Nyala Central Bank as the payroll cutoff took effect. SAF simultaneously extended its aerial campaign against RSF positions in Nyala to a fourth consecutive day (May 15–18), targeting Al-Masane weapons depots with Hemedti reportedly still in the city. The Darfur aerial offensive continues to pressure all RSF-held state capitals. The derecognition order complicates the Quad-proposed 90-day humanitarian truce framework by formally declaring the RSF a rebel group without state standing — hardening SAF's already maximalist position. Humanitarian conditions continue to deteriorate: 19.5 million Sudanese face acute food insecurity as of mid-May 2026 (WFP/FAO/UNICEF), with the UN projecting a lean-season peak of 28.9 million (June–August) and the 2026 humanitarian appeal only ~20% funded. The US House Foreign Affairs Committee's May 14 bipartisan 44–2 RSF genocide resolution adds US congressional pressure as the war enters its 38th month.
